findings.statement: The company has begun recovering IEEPA tariffs it paid: it received $184 in 2026, made up of $174 in refunds recorded as a reduction to merchandise costs and $10 as interest income, after the Supreme Court ruled the tariffs unlawful. This directly contradicts the idea that the duties cannot be clawed back.
findings.rationale: The filing states the ruling and the amounts actually received, so the claim that the duties are a pure cost with no recovery is not borne out for the IEEPA tariffs.

quotes.text: In February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that the IEEPA tariffs were unlawful.
During 2026, we began filing for refunds and received $184, made up of $174 in refunds, recorded as a reduction to merchandise costs, and $10 recorded as interest income.

findings.statement: Refunds continued after year end: $155 in additional refunds were received, and the company intends to invest the majority of refunds in increased value for the member.
findings.rationale: The further receipt shows recovery is ongoing, though the filing also says part of the refunds goes back to members in lower prices, so the retained benefit is smaller than the gross amount.

quotes.text: Subsequent to 2026, we received $155 in additional refunds and we intend to continue to invest the majority of the refunds in increased value for the member.

findings.statement: The refunds, net of the investment in price reductions for members, positively affected gross margin by three basis points, so the recovery had a small but visible effect on results.
findings.rationale: The effect is stated by the company and is small, which limits how strongly it undercuts the claim.

quotes.text: IEEPA tariff refunds, net of investment in price reductions for members, positively impacted gross margin by three basis points.

findings.statement: Management still describes tariffs as more likely to hurt than help results, which is consistent with duties being a cost while they are in force.
findings.rationale: This is a general statement about tariffs and does not address whether paid duties can be recovered, so it only partly supports the claim.

quotes.text: Higher tariffs are more likely to adversely impact rather than improve our results.

response.rationale: The claim is too absolute for the filing. For the IEEPA tariffs, the company reports that the Supreme Court ruled them unlawful, that it received refunds in 2026 and afterwards, and that they were recognized as a reduction to merchandise costs. Other duties are not discussed, and the general language about tariffs as a cost remains.
unknowns: How much of the approximately $500 of IEEPA tariffs paid will ultimately be refunded, and when.
How much of the refunds is kept versus returned to members through lower prices beyond the three basis point net effect.
Whether duties other than IEEPA tariffs can be recovered.
The outcome of the class actions alleging tariff costs were passed on to members, which could affect who is entitled to the refunds.
